{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint lacks explicit analysis for ORR in the statistical section",
      "quote": "Confirmed ORR according to RECIST v1.1, as assessed by ICR.",
      "page": 37,
      "section": "3 Objectives and Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The primary endpoint is defined in the objectives table, but the statistical analysis section (Table 17) does not explicitly state the analysis for the primary endpoint ORR as assessed by ICR. The table lists ORR but the note says 'All endpoints derived from RECIST use ICR and Investigator assessment', which is ambiguous. The primary endpoint analysis should be clearly specified.",
      "fix": "Add a clear statement in Section 9.4.1 that the primary analysis of ORR will be based on ICR assessment, with a two-sided 95% exact CI, and specify the analysis population (FAS)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing estimand attributes for primary endpoint",
      "quote": "Confirmed ORR according to RECIST v1.1, as assessed by ICR.",
      "page": 37,
      "section": "3 Objectives and Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The primary endpoint does not specify the estimand attributes: population (FAS is implied but not stated for the primary estimand), intercurrent events (e.g., how to handle death or progression before response), and summary measure (proportion with confirmed response). The protocol lacks a formal estimand section.",
      "fix": "Add an estimand section that defines the primary estimand for ORR, including the target population (FAS), the intercurrent event strategy (e.g., treatment discontinuation, death), and the summary measure (proportion with 95% CI)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Sample size justification lacks power and effect size",
      "quote": "A sample size of 100 patients has been determined to provide sufficient precision for the estimation of the ORR in this population",
      "page": 90,
      "section": "9.2 Sample Size Determination",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The sample size is based on precision of the CI, but no explicit power or effect size is provided. For a single-arm study, it is common to state the expected ORR and the width of the CI, but the protocol does not specify the target ORR or the desired precision. The table provides CIs for observed rates, but the justification is incomplete.",
      "fix": "State the assumed true ORR (e.g., 30%) and the corresponding 95% CI width that the sample size is designed to achieve, and justify the clinical relevance."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing handling of missing data for efficacy endpoints",
      "quote": "procedures for accounting for missing, unused, and spurious data",
      "page": 92,
      "section": "9.4 Statistical Analyses",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol mentions that the SAP will describe procedures for missing data, but the statistical section does not provide any details on how missing data will be handled for the primary or secondary efficacy endpoints. This is a gap in the protocol.",
      "fix": "Add a subsection on missing data handling, specifying the methods for each endpoint (e.g., for ORR, patients with missing response will be considered non-responders; for time-to-event, censoring rules)."
    },
    {
      "title": "No multiplicity adjustment for secondary endpoints",
      "quote": "To further evaluate the efficacy of T-DXd in patients with metastatic or unresectable tumors harboring pre-specified HER2 activating mutations across tumor types.",
      "page": 37,
      "section": "3 Objectives and Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol lists multiple secondary endpoints (DoR, DCR, PFS, OS, etc.) but does not describe any multiplicity control strategy. Since these are confirmatory secondary objectives, the risk of type I error inflation should be addressed.",
      "fix": "Add a section on multiplicity, either stating that secondary endpoints are tested hierarchically or that no formal adjustment is made and results are considered exploratory."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistency in analysis population for ORR",
      "quote": "Full analysis Set, Measurable Disease Analysis Set (8-patient interim futility evaluation only), Centrally-determined Efficacy Analysis Set (CEAS)",
      "page": 91,
      "section": "9.3 Populations for Analyses",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The table lists ORR to be analyzed in FAS, MDAS, and CEAS, but the primary endpoint is defined as ORR by ICR. The protocol does not specify which population is primary for the primary endpoint. The MDAS is only for interim futility, but the CEAS is for sensitivity. The primary analysis population should be clearly stated as FAS.",
      "fix": "Clarify that the primary analysis of ORR will be based on the FAS, with sensitivity analyses on CEAS if needed."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for 'Proportion of patients alive and progression-free at 6 and 12 months'",
      "quote": "Proportion of patients alive and progression-free at 6 and 12 months.",
      "page": 37,
      "section": "3 Objectives and Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "This endpoint is listed in the objectives, but the statistical analysis table (Table 17) only mentions 'The proportions of patients alive and progression-free at 6 and 12 months (Kaplan-Meier estimates) will also be presented.' This is present, but the analysis is not detailed in terms of how the proportion is derived (e.g., KM estimate at time point) and whether a CI is provided.",
      "fix": "Specify that the proportion will be estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method with a 95% CI, and define the time points precisely (e.g., 6 months = 26 weeks)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Sample size does not account for interim futility and tumor type caps",
      "quote": "Enrolment in a specific tumor type will be paused after 8 patients with Investigator-assessed measurable disease at baseline have been treated within that tumor type, until a decision has been made on whether to stop enrolment to that tumor type based on the interim futility evaluation.",
      "page": 90,
      "section": "9.2 Sample Size Determination",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The sample size of 100 is stated, but the interim futility design (stopping a tumor type if no response in first 8 patients) may reduce the actual sample size. The protocol does not discuss the impact of this design on the overall sample size or the precision of the ORR estimate.",
      "fix": "Add a note that the sample size may be reduced due to early stopping of tumor types, and that the precision of the ORR estimate may be affected; consider a sensitivity analysis."
    }
  ]
}
